- SUP-1 [supported]: A bounded transformation has explicit inputs, outputs and accessible checks covering its material requirements; merely mentioning tests does not establish coverage.
- SUP-2 [supported]: Relevant repository state can be inspected and a localized repair mechanism can be verified; repository size, familiar terminology and file count are not difficulty proxies.
- SUP-3 [supported]: Numerical or typed behavior has explicit interfaces, edge cases and tolerances, and the solver can validate the core computation; a test harness does not solve an unknown algorithm.
- SUP-4 [supported]: The failure mechanism and search boundary are supplied or readily inspectable, and the requested change fits the configured solver; multiple mechanical edits need not require stronger reasoning.
- SUP-5 [supported]: Behavioral reproduction has an accessible executable reference or complete specification covering edge cases; hidden grading alone is not such a reference.
- UNC-1 [uncertain]: Material semantic choices or interacting invariants remain unresolved, so several plausible implementations could differ in correctness.
- UNC-2 [uncertain]: The task requires completeness across coupled paths, asynchronous state, schemas or compatibility surfaces without a clear search boundary or sufficient visible coverage.
- LIM-1 [unsupported]: Exact information must be recovered from noisy visual or temporal media without an available reliable extraction mechanism.
- LIM-2 [unsupported]: Success requires inaccessible reference behavior, undocumented state or unknown configuration. Such obstacles may defeat either solver; unsupported does not imply capable success.

Configured solver: Claude Sonnet 5 at high effort is a general coding solver. Evaluate its fit to the actual mechanism and scope. Clear instructions and runnable tests help, but do not establish complete coverage or guarantee success. Large repository size alone is not difficult scope. Public research does not establish a universal Sonnet advantage for a task family.
Harness: mini-SWE-agent 2.0.0, Linux shell, repository inspection and edits, existing tests and self-written reproductions; one fresh attempt, high native reasoning effort, 150 model calls and USD 5 inference limit. Final hidden tests are unavailable to the solver. No retry or inherited patch from another model.
